newsitem.title: USA: New York NAPM Nov business index rose to 64.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: New York NAPM Nov business index rose to 64.9 pct.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index of New York-area business conditions rose to 64.9 percent in November from 61.8 percent in October.
"Purchasers continued to report that the quality of their suppliers was good," said a report issued with the index.
An index reading higher than 50 percent denotes growth, while a reading lower than 50 percent implies a contraction, the report said.
Specifically, business conditions in the non-manufacturing sector rose to 63.1 percent in November from 61.1 percent the month before.
Manufacturing-sector conditions "accelerated sharply" to 81.1 percent from 67.8 percent, according to the report.

"The November manufacturing improvement accompanied a pickup in purchasers and a noticeably faster delivery rate, which are somewhat contradictory for their regional business conditions implication," the report said.
The prices paid index read 47 percent in November compared to 49 percent the month before.
Almost 24 percent of NAPM-New York survey respondents said they expect a rise in their fourth-quarter hiring plans versus the same time last year, while 31 percent said they would be lower.
"Looking forward to the upcoming six months, purchasers' optimism remained high in November," NAPM-New York said.
